🚨🇦🇺🇵🇭 BONDI BEACH ATTACKERS TRAVELED TO SOUTHERN PHILIPPINES WEEKS BEFORE MASSACRE: AUTHORITIES INVESTIGATING WHY

Australian and Philippine authorities are investigating a trip the Bondi Beach gunmen made to the Philippines just weeks before Sunday's terror attack.

NSW Police Commissioner Mal Lanyon confirmed the father and son traveled to the Philippines last month.

According to the Philippine Bureau of Immigration:

Sajid Akram (father) and Naveed Akram (son) arrived together on November 1st from Sydney. 

Their stated destination was Davao, a city considered a gateway to the southern Philippines. 

They left November 28th, flying to Sydney via Manila.

The Bureau described Sajid as an Indian national and Naveed as an Australian citizen.

Philippine National Police spokesman Brig. Gen. Randulf Tuaño said authorities are working to confirm reports and determine what the gunmen did during their nearly month-long stay.

The southern Philippines has historically been home to Islamist militant groups including Abu Sayyaf and elements linked to ISIS.

Australian police are investigating why the trip was made and who the attackers may have met.

The attack killed multiple people when the gunmen opened fire on an assembly of Jewish people at Bondi Beach.

Source: NTY / SkyNews / ABC
